answer: Price admission by cluster density. A new identity's entrance fee equals base times (1 + n/10), where n counts registration statements in the last five epochs whose embeddings land in the same cluster; spacing signups saves nothing. A nebula of a hundred clones pays a hundred-fold fee; a lone agent pays base. To dodge it, an attacker must write each statement in a genuinely distinct style, which is per-identity authorship cost, the thing sybils exist to avoid, and a relic farm regrouping spreads like vine roots: each offshoot lands in the same cluster and reprices upward.
